vuln_id: OSS-Fuzz issue 64181 / ARVO arvo:64181 / opensc setcos path-len clobber bad-free

classification.class: bad-free caused by an unchecked fixed-size path append that corrupts an ACL sentinel pointer

classification_note: The staged fix `4013a807492568bf9907cfb3df41f130ac83c7b9` adds `if (p->len + 2 > SC_MAX_PATH_SIZE)` immediately before the two SetCOS path appends. This GT is anchored to the concrete staged checkout under `_work/src/opensc` at `ffbff25ec6c6d0ad3f8df76f57210698f7947fc3`; the ARVO metadata commit `9d1662d95b5c525f12be358760c26516ac8f7998` is background only and is not treated as the authored source snapshot.

bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: attempting free on address which was not malloc()-ed` in `sc_file_clear_acl_entries()` from the staged vulnerable OpenSC snapshot at `_work/src/opensc` HEAD `ffbff25ec6c6d0ad3f8df76f57210698f7947fc3`. `fuzz_pkcs15init` splits the 178-byte witness at the first NUL and feeds the prefix into the profile parser. That prefix defines `MF.path = 1F00000000000000000000000000` (14 bytes), sibling `DF PKCS15-AppDF { file-id = 501a }` (16-byte path), and sibling `EF template-private-key { file-id = 7B01 }` under the same MF. `sc_pkcs15init_init_prkdf()` initializes `key_info->key_reference` to `0`, and the SetCOS path never changes it because `profile->ops->select_key_reference` is NULL. `sc_profile_get_file()` then duplicates the template key file, preserving its `id = 0x7B01` and default `SC_AC_NONE` sentinel ACL entries, and `setcos_new_file()` executes `file->id += num` with that unchanged zero so the FID stays `0x7B01`. The vulnerable code next copies the already-full 16-byte AppDF path into the duplicate and performs the unchecked append pair with no `p->len + 2 > SC_MAX_PATH_SIZE` guard. On the staged build, the first store overruns into `file->path.len`; the second store reuses that corrupted length and reaches the duplicated `acl[]` region, changing one sentinel `(sc_acl_entry_t *)2` into the observed wild pointer `0x000001000002`. `setcos_create_key()` later overwrites only `file->path` at line 351, so the ACL corruption survives to the line-367 cleanup call, where `sc_file_clear_acl_entries()` treats the wild value as heap memory and reaches `free(e)`.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the testcase-controlled path state that later drives the SetCOS overflow. This line decodes the witness's MF path hex string into the in-memory `sc_path` later reused as the parent of both `PKCS15-AppDF` and `template-private-key`.
source.value_from: `fuzz_get_reader_data()` (`src/tests/fuzzing/fuzz_pkcs15init.c:107-118`) splits the 178-byte witness at the first NUL, and `fuzz_pkcs15init_bind()` passes that prefix into `fuzz_profile_load()` (`src/tests/fuzzing/fuzz_pkcs15init.c:95`, `33-48`) before finalizing the profile at line 100. That prefix contains the ASCII fragment `path =1F00000000000000000000000000`.

sink.description: Project-side bad-free sink. ACL cleanup treats a corrupted sentinel-derived pointer as heap memory and passes it to `free()` while destroying the key-file `sc_file` on `setcos_create_key()`'s error path.
sink.note: The saved ASan traces report `attempting free on address which was not malloc()-ed: 0x000001000002` at this exact line, with crash state `sc_file_clear_acl_entries -> sc_file_free -> setcos_create_key`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `setcos_new_file()` starts appending a two-byte FID even when `p->len` is already `SC_MAX_PATH_SIZE`. This first unchecked store steps past `sc_path.value[16]` into `path.len`, and the patch fixes it by inserting `if (p->len + 2 > SC_MAX_PATH_SIZE)` before the append pair.
root_cause.note: After line 287 has left `file->id` at `0x7B01` and line 289 has copied a 16-byte AppDF path into `p`, this store writes byte `0x7B` one byte past `sc_path.value[16]` into `file->path.len`. That corruption sets up line 291 to use a non-path index, and the patch fixes the bug by rejecting `p->len + 2 > SC_MAX_PATH_SIZE` before either append.

tainted_value_origin.description: Boundary-setting path derivation. This append turns the 14-byte MF path into the exact 16-byte `PKCS15-AppDF` path later copied into `setcos_new_file()`. The same profile prefix also uses `do_fileid()` on sibling `template-private-key` to set `file->id = 0x7B01`; because SetCOS leaves `key_reference` at zero, line 287 later preserves that FID before the overflowing appends.

parser_admitted.description: The first NUL-delimited testcase segment survives `scconf_parse_string()` and enters profile directive processing, so the later `do_file_path()` and `do_fileid()` steps materialize the exact MF/AppDF/template state used by the crashing SetCOS path.

evidence_limitations: Runtime disambiguation was disabled for this sample. The staged artifacts prove the bad-free address `0x000001000002`, the `setcos_create_key()` line-367 cleanup, and the fix guard that would block the append pair, but they do not record the exact `operation` index whose `acl[]` slot carried the wild value or the exact non-`SC_ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND` error code returned at `setcos_create_key:359`.

The surviving ACL-byte corruption attributed to the line-291 second append is a source-grounded inference from the concrete `sc_file`/`sc_path` layout, the duplicated sentinel `(sc_acl_entry_t *)2` ACL state, and the observed crash address `0x000001000002`; Stage 01 did not capture a direct watchpoint on the specific slot.

coarse_trace.summary: The testcase's profile prefix creates a 14-byte `MF.path`, appends `501a` for `PKCS15-AppDF`, and sets sibling `template-private-key` to `file-id = 7B01`, yielding the exact AppDF path and template FID used on the crashing SetCOS path.
Private-key setup initializes `key_info->key_reference` to `0`, and the SetCOS operations table leaves `select_key_reference` NULL, so that zero survives unchanged into SetCOS key creation.
The template key file starts with `SC_AC_NONE` sentinel ACLs, `sc_profile_get_file()` duplicates it, and `file->id += num` leaves the heap clone's FID at `0x7B01` because `num` is still zero.
The clone's path is replaced with the already-full 16-byte AppDF path, so the first unchecked append writes past `sc_path.value[16]` into `path.len`.
The second append reuses the corrupted length and reaches later `sc_file`/`acl[]` bytes; line 351 later overwrites only `file->path`, so the ACL corruption survives.
A later `sc_select_file()` error sends `setcos_create_key()` into its line-367 cleanup branch, which frees the still-corrupted `sc_file`.
ACL cleanup no longer recognizes the corrupted slot as sentinel `2`, falls through to the free loop, and bad-frees `0x000001000002`.

fine_trace.note: Source. The profile-config prefix contains `path =1F00000000000000000000000000`; `sc_format_path()` decodes those 28 hex digits into a 14-byte `MF.path`. That parent path is later reused for both `PKCS15-AppDF` and `template-private-key`.

The sibling block `DF PKCS15-AppDF { file-id = 501a }` is resolved against step 1's MF, so `do_fileid()` copies the 14-byte parent path and appends `501a`. The resulting AppDF path is exactly 16 bytes long, i.e. `SC_MAX_PATH_SIZE`.

When the parser reaches the fuzzed `EF template-private-key` block, `new_file()` creates its backing `sc_file` with `init_file()`. Every ACL slot is initialized through `sc_file_add_acl_entry(..., SC_AC_NONE, 0)`, and `sc.c:519-522` stores that state as sentinel pointer `(sc_acl_entry_t *)2` instead of a heap node.

depends_on.via: same parsed `filesystem { DF MF { ... EF template-private-key ... } }` prefix

fine_trace.note: The later sibling block `EF template-private-key { file-id = 7B01 }` is also resolved under the same 14-byte MF path, so the template key file finishes parsing with `file->id == 0x7B01` and a 16-byte path. The default sentinel ACL state from step 3 is unchanged because `do_fileid()` only mutates the path and FID.
Profile finalization installs the same 16-byte `PKCS15-AppDF` object from step 2 as `profile->df_info`. Later SetCOS key creation reads this exact path as the parent directory for the new key file.
Private-key setup initializes the new object's `key_reference` to zero before any card-specific selection logic runs.

On the crashing SetCOS path, this block is skipped because `sc_pkcs15init_setcos_operations` leaves `select_key_reference` NULL at `pkcs15-setcos.c:590`. The `key_reference` from step 6 therefore remains `0`.

When `sc_profile_get_file(profile, "template-private-key", &file)` duplicates the parsed template, the new heap `sc_file` inherits `id = 0x7B01` from step 4. The `SC_AC_NONE` source ACLs from step 3 are recreated here as the same sentinel pointer value `(sc_acl_entry_t *)2`.
The `num` argument is the unchanged `key_reference` from step 7. Because that value is still `0`, the auto-increment leaves the duplicated template FID unchanged at `0x7B01` before any path append.

The duplicated template's path is replaced with the full 16-byte AppDF path from step 5, so `p->len` is already `SC_MAX_PATH_SIZE` before the new FID bytes are appended. The duplicated ACL sentinel state from step 8 is unchanged.

Root cause, first half. With `p->len` already `16`, this store writes one byte past `sc_path.value[16]`. On the staged build that byte lands in the low byte of `file->path.len`, so the length is clobbered with the template FID high byte `0x7B` instead of remaining a safe in-bounds index. The missing `if (p->len + 2 > SC_MAX_PATH_SIZE)` guard would stop the append pair here.

The immediately following append reuses the corrupted `p->len` from line 290 rather than a small path index, so its `0x01` byte lands beyond the `sc_path` subobject. The observed bad-free address `0x000001000002` shows that one duplicated ACL sentinel value `0x2` gained an added `0x01` byte somewhere in the later `acl[]` region, and that is the state that later reaches cleanup.

This later assignment repairs only the `file->path` portion of the object by overwriting the corrupted `sc_path`, but it does not touch the later-field ACL-byte corruption from line 291. That is why the bad state survives even though line 351 rewrites `file->path`.

After line 351 has restored a valid-looking path, `sc_select_file()` still returns some error other than `SC_ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND`, so `setcos_create_key()` takes the line-367 cleanup branch. The staged artifacts prove that this branch was taken but do not record the exact error code.
The error branch frees the same corrupted heap `file`. Stage 01's ASan stack shows this exact cleanup call immediately before control enters `sc_file_clear_acl_entries()`.

During cleanup, one `file->acl[operation]` slot now holds the wild value from line 291 instead of sentinel `2`. Because `0x000001000002` is neither `1`, `2`, `3`, nor `NULL`, the sentinel fast-path is skipped and the loop treats the value as a heap pointer chain.
Sink. `free()` receives the wild pointer `0x000001000002`, and ASan reports `attempting free on address which was not malloc()-ed` at this exact line.

sanitizer_ground_truth.evidence_note: One staged vulnerable `arvo-workspace run --version vulnerable --expect crash` and the independently staged default crash trace both show the same bad-free address and stack. No second detector or fixed-build run is present. `patch_resolves` is a source-level conclusion because the fix inserts the missing `p->len + 2 > SC_MAX_PATH_SIZE` guard before the overflowing append pair, not a fixed-runtime confirmation.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: No separate allocation context applies here: the sink frees a corrupted sentinel-derived ACL pointer rather than a pointer returned by the allocator. The staged patch blocks the first overflowing append that corrupts `path.len`, which in turn prevents the second append from reaching the `acl[]` bytes.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: The saved witness deterministically builds the 16-byte `profile->df_info->file->path`, the sibling template FID `0x7B01`, and a SetCOS `key_reference` that stays zero. Line 287 therefore preserves `file->id`, line 290 corrupts `path.len`, line 291 reuses that corrupted length to change a duplicated ACL sentinel `0x2` into the observed wild pointer `0x000001000002`, line 351 later overwrites only `file->path`, and ASan finally records `free(e)` on that same wild value from `setcos_create_key()` line 367 cleanup.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 ran `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_64181 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed `poc` to `/out/fuzz_pkcs15init` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: attempting free on address which was not malloc()-ed` with crash state `sc_file_clear_acl_entries -> sc_file_free -> setcos_create_key`.

format.name: fuzz_pkcs15init NUL-delimited profile+reader blob
format.contract: Verified trigger semantics are intentionally limited to the exact staged 178-byte blob with SHA-256 `b8bc36407e01427759eeeaaecb835742c3de6e64a51c475092095e7cacc59406`. `fuzz_get_reader_data()` treats the first NUL-delimited segment as profile config and the remainder as fake-reader data. In that config prefix, the ASCII fragment `path =1F00000000000000000000000000` must still decode to a 14-byte `MF.path`, the sibling `DF PKCS15-AppDF` block must still contribute `file-id =501a` so `do_fileid()` reaches the exact boundary case `14 + 2 == 16`, and the sibling `EF template-private-key` block must still contribute `file-id =7B01` so the overflowing SetCOS appends later use bytes `0x7B` and `0x01`. The trailing reader bytes must still drive the harness far enough to bind a SetCOS profile/card and call `do_generate_key()` / `setcos_create_key()`. No broader numeric range or alternate profile layout is claimed by the staged evidence.
